root_idea.summary: The root centers on breaking or crushing a thing into pieces.
root_idea.development: From breaking and crushing develop usages for things broken by dryness, agents or forces that crush, crowding that presses people together, and figurative effects such as infirmity, drought, or ravage.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed as the normalized nominal citation form حُطَامٌ.
Displayed as the normalized nominal citation form حُطَمَةٌ.

senses.definition: To crush or break into pieces.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic use is transitive, describing the crushing of one thing by another; the lexical branch includes breaking, bruising, or pressing by force.

senses.definition: Broken fragments or debris, especially material made dry and brittle.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the word is used of vegetation or crops reduced to dry fragments.

senses.definition: The Crusher: a vehement fire that breaks apart everything cast into it; an epithet for Hellfire.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, حُطَمَةٌ is the name or وصف of the Hellfire, presented as a fire that crushes what it receives.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break or become broken into pieces, particularly when said of a dry or tough thing such as a bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease affecting a beast’s legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical noun for the condition, not merely the verbal noun of breaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An aged, emaciated, or weakened beast or horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended description associated with deterioration through age.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing that breaks into pieces of itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjectival description of the thing undergoing the breaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break something into pieces or crush it severely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II, with an intensive or extensive force nuance relative to the basic transitive branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To spoil or damage pasture by grazing over it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional transitive use referring to destructive grazing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone a broken or infirm old person, or to make someone infirm through age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative or extended transitive use associated with burdens or advancing age.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break apart or crumble.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V intransitive use, including things breaking into pieces and earth crumbling from excessive dryness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For people to crowd or press together, crushing or bruising one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V reciprocal or collective use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become inflamed with anger or rage against someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative Form V construction with عَلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who breaks through ranks to the right and left.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent noun describing forceful penetration of a formation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The crowding, thronging, or pressing of people, including their pushing one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for collective pressure or crush.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A surge or main thrust of a torrent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical use for the forceful advancing portion of a flood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The havoc wrought by a lion among cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for destructive crushing or ravaging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dearth, drought, or sterility; also a year characterized by such conditions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use based on the notion of breaking or destroying everything.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fragment, or what is broken into pieces, of a dry or tough thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural may refer collectively to broken pieces; the expression can describe a broken spear-shaft and its portions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A voracious or insatiable eater.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use likening the eater to a fire that consumes and breaks everything.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large herd of camels or sheep and goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is associated with the herd crushing herbage and the ground with its feet and feeding destructively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A harsh or ungentle herdsman who drives animals so that they crush or bruise one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative occupational description based on violent driving or pasturing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Coats of mail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is variously explained as referring to their maker or user, their ability to break swords, or their heaviness and breadth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fragments of an egg or pieces of an eggshell.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional noun use distinct from the Quranic application to dry vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The frail or perishing goods and possessions of the present world.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression emphasizing the transient, breakable character of worldly goods.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lion that crushes everything it devours; also a wind that crushes everything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive agent description applied to a destructive animal or force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dry, broken herbage left from the preceding year.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The condition is attributed to dryness and breaking into pieces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A part of the precinct of the Kaaba, especially the Ḥijr or its enclosing wall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions of its precise boundaries vary; the name is connected either with its being left broken or with people crowding and pressing there.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A digestive, or something that aids digestion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate lexical item; it is not assigned as a meaning of حُطَمَةٌ or حُطْمَةٌ.

cautions: The torrent-surge meaning of حَطْمَةٌ is lexically reported, but its derivation from this root is questioned in the root-level evidence.
The digestive meaning belongs to حَاطُومٌ as a separate lexical item and is not a meaning of حُطَمَةٌ or حُطْمَةٌ.
